cleanIntro: Davide Pedersoli's Muzzleloading Guns owner's manual gives the side-by-side smooth bore shotgun its own chapter on pages 22 to 26, separate from the single-shot guns and separate again from the rifled Kodiak and Safari express doubles on pages 27 to 30. That separation matters at the back end: on a single-shot Pedersoli the breech plug is a serviceable joint with its own removal procedure, and on this shotgun it is not. What comes apart is the barrel from the stock at the wedges, the nipples out of the drums, and nothing else. Two barrels also means two ignition trains, and most of what follows exists to stop you confusing them.

steps.title: Both barrels unloaded, muzzles safe, before anything moves
steps.action: A muzzleloader has no chamber to look into, so 'unloaded' means proved unloaded on both barrels — hammers down, no caps on either nipple, and the ramrod dropped down each bore against your own load marks to confirm nothing is sitting on a powder charge. Pedersoli opens the side-by-side chapter with this instruction because everything that follows assumes it. A double that is half loaded looks exactly like a double that is empty.
steps.prose: If a mark shows a charge still down there, that is the loading-mistake procedure on page 24, not a cleaning job.
steps.quote: WARNING: BEFORE PROCEEDING ALWAYS MAKE SURE THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Loading and shooting instructions for side by side muzzle loading smooth bore shotguns, p.22
steps.warn: Both barrels. Both nipples. Caps off before anything else.

steps.title: One cap at a time, and never both hammers at half cock
steps.action: Get the capping discipline straight before you handle the gun cold, because it is the same discipline that keeps you safe at the bench. Pedersoli's rule for this shotgun is one cap on the gun at any moment, with one hammer at half cock and the other fully down — never both hammers at half cock together. The second cap only goes on after the first barrel has actually been fired.
steps.prose: Two capped nipples under two hammers is what turns a jarred hammer into a double discharge.
steps.quote: (NEVER PLACE BOTH HAMMERS AT HALF COCK POSITION AT THE SAME TIME), place the first cap; PLACE JUST ONE CAP AT A TIME, you can place the second one only after having fired the first barrel.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Loading, point 10f, p.24
steps.warn: CAUTION: NEVER RELOAD A FIRED BARREL WITHOUT REMOVING CAP FROM THE OTHER.

steps.title: Never drop a hammer on a bare nipple
steps.action: When you let the hammers down to the fired position, lower them under thumb control onto a spent cap or onto a nipple protector — never let one fall on a bare nipple. The nipple is a small hardened cone with a narrow flash channel, and a hammer striking it directly peens the cone and closes that channel, which is a misfire you will chase for months. Pedersoli states the rule plainly for percussion arms.
steps.prose: The same paragraph gives the flintlock equivalent — never let the hammer fall on the frizzen without a flint — which tells you the maker regards this as a first-order handling rule, not a nicety.
steps.caution: A peened nipple is a misfire that looks like bad powder.
steps.quote: 7) Never let the hammer on a percussion firearm fall without a cap on nipple or it will damage the nipple. On a flintlock arm, never let the hammer fall on the frizzen without a flint in the hammer.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Important cautions for muzzle loading shooting, point 7, p.12

steps.title: Ramrod out, then the wedges
steps.action: Pull the ramrod clear of its thimbles first — the barrels cannot lift with it in place, and levering against a trapped rod splits the forend. Then retract the wedge or wedges that pass through the stock and the barrel lugs, driving them from the direction they went in. They are a light interference fit, so they should move under a brass or nylon drift with hand pressure, not hammer blows.
steps.prose: Pedersoli's line of muzzleloaders splits into two groups — barrels that end in a breech plug screwed to the tang, and barrels with a hook breech. The side-by-side shotgun is the wedge-and-hook kind.
steps.caution: Steel drift on a wedge marks the stock inlet. Use brass or nylon.
steps.quote: 2c) For the guns of the seconds group, the barrel is fixed to the stock with wedges. Once removed the ramrod, retract the wedge or wedges, handle the barrel at the muzzle and rotate towards the height, the lug will disengage from its seat.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — How to remove the barrel from stock, point 2c, p.20

steps.title: Lift the barrels off the hook
steps.action: With the wedges out, take the barrels at the muzzle and rotate them upward. The hook at the breech disengages from its seat in the tang as the muzzles rise, and the whole barrel assembly comes free of the stock in one piece. Lift, do not pull straight forward — the hook is a rotating joint and dragging it out sideways bruises both the hook and the tang seat it has to index against for the rest of the gun's life.
steps.prose: You are now holding two chromed smooth bores joined at the ribs, with two drums and two nipples at the breech.
steps.quote: handle the barrel at the muzzle and rotate towards the height, the lug will disengage from its seat.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — How to remove the barrel from stock, point 2c, p.20

steps.title: Nipples out — and that is where the strip stops
steps.action: Back both nipples out of their drums with the correct nipple wrench so hot water can flow through the flash channels rather than stopping against a blocked cone. This is the only part Pedersoli asks you to take out of this shotgun's breech. The breech plug behind it stays where it is: on the side-by-side the maker states flatly that it cannot be removed, even though the same booklet gives a breech plug removal procedure for single-shot rifles and pistols on page 21.
steps.prose: Do not read the single-shot breech-plug section as though it applied here. The shotgun chapter overrides it in one line.
steps.quote: Percussion rifles or pistols: remove the nipple.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Cleaning instructions for single shot muzzle loading guns, Cleaning, p.21
steps.warn: On the side by side: ATTENTION: the breech plug CANNOT BE REMOVED.

steps.title: PROHIBITED — the drum and the breech plug do not come out
steps.action: If a ball or a wad is stuck part-way down a bore, the temptation is to open the back of the barrel and push it out. Pedersoli forbids that outright, for any gun in this booklet. The way out is a screw-tip bullet puller of the right calibre from the muzzle, with black powder solvent poured in to soften whatever fouling is holding the projectile. Opening the breech instead is how a shotgun barrel gets scrapped and a shooter gets hurt.
steps.prose: The shotgun chapter says the same thing again in its own words at the cleaning section — the breech plug cannot be removed.
steps.quote: UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES SHOULD THE INDIVIDUAL ATTEMPT TO REMOVE THE PERCUSSION DRUM OR BREECH PLUG FROM THE FIREARM.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Important cautions for muzzle loading shooting, point 17, p.12
steps.warn: This prohibition bars a teardown. It does NOT bar cleaning — the whole cleaning sequence below is done with the breech plug in place.

steps.title: Hot soapy water through both bores, same day
steps.action: Black powder residue is hygroscopic and corrosive, and it starts working on chromed steel within hours, so this happens the day you shoot, not the weekend after. Stand the breech end of the barrels in hot water with a black powder detergent and pump a tight patch or a bristle brush down each bore in turn; the water draws up through the open nipple seats and out again as you stroke. Do both barrels, and wipe the drums, the ribs and the underside where fouling collects out of sight.
steps.prose: Pedersoli notes these shotgun bores are chromed, and then sends you to the single-shot cleaning procedure unchanged.
steps.aside: 12f) Our shotguns have chromed barrel bores, however the same procedures seen at point 2c and at “CLEANING” of section “CLEANING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SINGLE SHOT MUZZLE LOADING GUNS” in this booklet, are to be followed.
steps.quote: Scrub bore with hot soapy water or in hot water with specific detergent (item USA 487) and wipe all powder fouling from all other metallic parts too.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Cleaning instructions for single shot muzzle loading guns, Cleaning, p.21

steps.title: Flush hot, dry hot, oil as it cools
steps.action: Rinse both bores with the hottest clean water you can run to carry the soap out, then dry them immediately with fresh patches while the steel is still hot — the residual heat drives the last moisture out of the flash channels and the drum threads where a patch cannot reach. Oil the bores and every metal surface as soon as the barrels cool. Leaving them to cool wet is how a set of chromed bores gets pitted at the breech end in a single week.
steps.prose: Hot metal dries itself. Cold metal holds a film of water in exactly the places you cannot see.
steps.caution: Oil the barrel lightly as soon as it cools inside and out. Apply a coat of oil to all metallic parts too.
steps.quote: Dry barrel and all metallic parts rapidly with fresh patches while they are still hot.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Cleaning instructions for single shot muzzle loading guns, Cleaning, p.21

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The barrels are off the stock, both nipples are out, both bores are clean, dry and oiled, and the breech plugs have never moved. That is the whole of the strip Pedersoli publishes for a side-by-side percussion shotgun. Deep Clean covers the nipple seats, the lock and the choke tubes if yours is fitted for them, plus the reassembly order that keeps the wedges holding tension.
steps.prose: Refit the nipples before the barrels go back so you are not fighting them in the stock.
steps.quote: Replace the nipple (on percussion models), or vent (on flintlock models).
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Cleaning instructions for single shot muzzle loading guns, Cleaning, p.21

deepSteps.title: Nipple seats and drums — clean, do not dismantle
deepSteps.action: With the nipples out, clean the seats and the flash channels with a pipe cleaner and solvent so both barrels light at the same speed. Work on the seat and the channel only; the drum itself stays screwed into the barrel. When the nipples go back, run them down to snug and stop — Pedersoli's warning about excessive force on drum and nipple threads applies whenever these small parts are handled, and a stripped nipple thread in a shotgun drum is not a field repair.
deepSteps.prose: Uneven flash channels are the usual reason one barrel of a double feels slower on the trigger than the other.
deepSteps.quote: When reassembling the drum and the nipple do not apply an excessive strength, or you may break the parts.
deepSteps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — How to remove the breech plug from barrel, p.21
deepSteps.warn: Clean the drum. Do not remove the drum.

deepSteps.title: Choke tubes, if your shotgun takes them
deepSteps.action: A Pedersoli side-by-side may be threaded for interchangeable chokes. Take each tube out, clean the threads in the muzzle and on the tube, grease them lightly and run the tube back down until it is properly tight — a tube that backs out under recoil will damage the muzzle and the tube together. Check them again part way through a long day of shooting rather than assuming they stayed put, which is the maker's own advice.
deepSteps.prose: Never change a tube on a loaded gun: on a muzzleloader that means an unproved bore is pointing at your hands while you work at the muzzle.
deepSteps.caution: We do not recommend chokes tighter than improved-cylinder for steel shot.
deepSteps.quote: Never change choke tubes on a loaded firearm.
deepSteps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Double barrel shotgun with interchangeable choke tubes, p.26

deepSteps.title: Dry the bores out before the first load of the day
deepSteps.action: Oil left in a muzzleloading bore contaminates the first powder charge and can kill ignition or hang the shot. Pedersoli's remedy for this shotgun is to cap both nipples with the gun pointed safe and snap the hammers two or three times before loading, which blows the oil film out of the breech ends and off the nipples. Repeat it until the caps sound sharp and consistent on both barrels.
deepSteps.prose: A dull, muffled cap is oil in the channel. A crisp one means the train is dry.
deepSteps.quote: 5f) With the gun pointing in a safe direction place caps on the nipples, set the hammers in full position and fire. This operation should be repeated two or three times in order to dry out the base of bores and the nipples.
deepSteps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Loading, point 5f, p.22
deepSteps.warn: Muzzle in a safe direction — the gun is not inert while you do this.

cleaning.name: BARRELS AND BORES
tasks: Clean the same day you shoot — black powder fouling is corrosive
Nipples out of both drums before water goes near the barrels
Hot soapy water or hot water with black powder detergent (item USA 487) through both bores
Flush with the hottest clean water available to carry the soap out
Dry both bores and every metal part with fresh patches WHILE STILL HOT
Oil the bores and all metal as soon as they cool

cleaning.name: IGNITION — PERCUSSION
tasks: Clean both nipple seats and flash channels; refit the nipples snug, never forced
PROHIBITED: do not remove the drum or the breech plug from the firearm
Never let a hammer fall on a bare nipple

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBES (IF FITTED)
tasks: Never change tubes on a loaded firearm
Clean and lightly grease the muzzle and tube threads
Make sure the tube is properly tightened before shooting, and re-check it during a long session
No choke tighter than improved cylinder with steel shot

cleaning.name: STOCK AND FURNITURE
tasks: Wipe fouling from the lock plates, hammers and tang
Check the barrel channel and wedge holes are dry before the barrels go back

reassembly: Refit both nipples to their drums, snug only — excessive force breaks the parts.
Hook the barrel breech into the tang and confirm it seats properly before the barrels come down.
Lower the barrels into the stock channel — do not force barrel into stock.
The barrels must fit with a minimal amount of tension so the wedges are held in.
Gently insert the wedges RIGHT TO LEFT, then refit the ramrod.
fncheck: With both nipples fitted and no caps on the gun, work each hammer to half cock and to full cock and confirm it holds at both, one lock at a time. Check the barrels sit down hard in the stock with the wedges home and no gap at the tang, and that the ramrod runs freely in its thimbles. Then cap both nipples, point the gun in a safe direction, and snap the hammers two or three times to dry the bores and prove both ignition trains fire crisply before any powder goes down a barrel.
